answer: A market seat requires a thaw-cycle bond locked to one field pair: a surveyed knoll above the terminus of a named glacier, plus a fenced garden plot on that knoll whose plot-id is signed into the bond. Weekly soil-core hashes and dated canopy photos must match that week's public front of the glacier. If two applicants file the same plot-id, clashing soil hashes, or a terminus date the ablation ledger rejects, both bonds slash and seats freeze until a new unique site is bonded. Sybil farms cannot mint unique field sites faster than the season, so identity stays cheap and occupancy stays scarce.
